content_preview.title: GitHub Makes Agentic Workflows and Copilot Fusion Generally Available and Rolls Out Shared Copilot Automations in October 28 Changelog Entries
content_preview.summary: GitHub's October 28 changelog entries describe general availability for Agentic Workflows and Copilot Fusion, shared Copilot Automations, and a public preview of Copilot Projects.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

GitHub published several changelog entries dated October 28, 2026 covering its coding-agent products. According to the [GitHub changelog](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-10-28-github-agentic-workflows-generally-available), GitHub Agentic Workflows, "an open source project from GitHub Next, is now generally available." A separate [entry on Copilot Fusion](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-10-28-route-and-orchestrate-models-with-github-copilot-fusion) says that feature is also gen...

editor_notes.content_quality: Clear News piece (694 words, range 400-1200) organised per changelog entry (Agentic Workflows, Shared Automations, Fusion, Projects/computer use) with an Overview and a What We Don't Know section. Title is 142 characters (cap 150). Headline status wording matches the entries: Agentic Workflows 'is now generally available' (entry 0), Copilot Fusion 'is generally available' (entry 2), Shared Copilot Automations 'are rolling out' (entry 1), Projects 'now in public preview' and computer use 'in public preview on macOS and Windows' (entry 3). The title does not overstate: it says 'Rolls Out' for Automations, matching the entry, and does not call Projects GA (Projects appear only in the summary as public preview).
editor_notes.source_verification: Read all 4 gzipped snapshots (source-0..3.html.gz), all HTTP 200, suspicious_patterns null for all, then re-fetched each live URL with curl (HTTP 200) and compared extracted article text with the snapshot: identical for all four, so no drift. All four are github.blog changelog entries dated October 28, 2026; github.blog is on config/source_allowlist.txt (line 889). Entry 0 (Agentic Workflows GA): verified 'an open source project from GitHub Next, is now generally available' verbatim; use cases (issue triage, CI failure analysis, documentation updates, test writing); natural-language Markdown compiled to Actions YAML; reuse of runner groups and policy constraints; Copilot or bring-your-own agent; five safeguards (integrity filter rules, read-only by default, sandboxed container behind Agent Workflow Firewall, safe outputs, threat detection job); GA additions (ARC with Docker-in-Docker, gh aw forecast no longer experimental with threat detection credits and monthly ranges, per-workflow model providers, model router, Cloud Hypervisor or NVX micro-VM and enclaves); availability on github.com for Free, Team, Enterprise and Copilot license needed for default Copilot CLI engine. All match. The article omits the Accenture testimonial (only a customer quote; omission is neutral). Entry 1 (Automations): 'Shared Copilot Automations are rolling out' ; read/write visibility; the quoted sentence 'AI credits are billed to the organization or user that owns the repository, rather than to the person who created the automation.' is verbatim; attributed to Copilot; belongs to repository; Shared under Type, type cannot be changed; plans Pro, Pro+, Max, Business, Enterprise. All match (article omits the 'availability may vary' line and the org-owned-repository admin policy requirement; incompleteness, not error). Entry 2 (Fusion): 'GitHub Copilot Fusion is generally available'; Standard/High/Max effort levels; Single/Cascade/Critique patterns (article paraphrases 'quality check' as 'quality assessment', unquoted, acceptable); the quote 'within two points of Claude Code with Opus 5.5 Max' verified verbatim in raw HTML text, in a GitHub-voiced sentence: 'In the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index, Copilot Fusion Max scored 60, within two points of Claude Code with Opus 5.5 Max. It delivered that result at about half the average API cost per task, using about half as many tokens and taking about 40% less time per task.' Article's score 60, half cost, half tokens, about 40% less time all correct. The entry gives no Claude Code score, no test conditions and no link to the index, and the article does not invent any. Billing (each model's standard rate; limited-time 30% discount for paid plans), availability on all Copilot plans in VS Code, Copilot app, Copilot CLI, JetBrains, and admin model policies/default via enterprise managed settings all match. Entry 3 (Projects): 'Copilot Projects are now in public preview' verbatim; multi-repository or no repository; many agents returning results such as PRs; computer use in public preview on macOS and Windows; approval before controlling an app; org can disable via managed settings. All match. No orphan URLs: every body link is in article.sources. Independence: all four sources are GitHub first-party; no independent confirmation exists in the cited material and the article says so.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every number, status, plan list, quote and date traces to the raw HTML of the cited entries. The one direct quote about Claude Code is verbatim and attributed to GitHub ('The entry reports'); the benchmark is named (Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index) as GitHub reports it, and the article states 'These figures appear in GitHub's own announcement' and, in What We Don't Know, that they lack independent confirmation. Note the index is a third-party benchmark but the Fusion Max result and cost comparison are reported only by GitHub; the article handles this correctly. Minor: the Overview says 'several changelog entries' and Projects are covered as a fourth entry; the 'Rolls Out ... Changelog Entries' title and summary are consistent with the body.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral, descriptive and attributed (According to GitHub, GitHub says, The entry reports). No promotional adjectives or Herald evaluation. Nothing disparaging or promotional is added about Anthropic's Claude Code or Opus; the comparison appears only inside the attributed quote. Neutrality toward GitHub/Microsoft versus other AI tool vendors maintained; vendor customer testimonials (Accenture, AT&T) were left out rather than repeated.
editor_notes.originality: Not a duplicate. Existing coverage is adjacent: 2026-10/05 (Copilot CLI and app computer use public preview) and 2026-10/06 (Copilot dynamic workflows). This article covers different announcements (Agentic Workflows GA, Fusion GA, shared Automations) and only mentions computer use briefly in the Universe releases entry; no suppression needed. Curated related_articles added for the two adjacent Copilot articles.
concerns: Conflict of interest disclosure: the article names Anthropic's product (Claude Code) and model (Opus 5.5 Max) in a GitHub benchmark claim. Anthropic makes the model powering this newsroom's writer and reviewer (Claude). Reviewed with strict neutrality: the claim is clearly GitHub's, verbatim, attributed, flagged as unconfirmed, and no Herald-originated comparison, praise or criticism was added. No impact on verdict.
First-party only: all four sources are GitHub changelog entries; no independent confirmation of the Fusion benchmark, cost figures or the GA/rollout claims; the article discloses this.
Minor omissions (not errors): 'availability may vary as the rollout progresses' and the org admin policy for shared automations in organization-owned repos.
recommendations: For follow-ups, seek an independent source (Artificial Analysis index page or third-party testing) for the Fusion Max score and cost comparison.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, carefully attributed first-party news roundup; all status wordings, figures, plans and the one quote verified against raw HTML snapshots and live re-fetch. Title length 142/150. No corrections needed. Featured candidacy: 2 - GitHub Copilot's model-routing GA and agentic workflows GA matter to a broad developer audience, but first-party-only sourcing and an incremental product-update nature keep it below exceptional
